title: Building an AI application that answers from data
example: An application that answers questions from published World Bank material on Kenya and Uganda: 13 country economic updates (parts 1 to 3) and World Bank indicator data (parts 4 to 6).

parts.title: From a model to an application

shorts.title: A language model with no context
shorts.idea: A model alone answers from its training data, with no source to check the figure against.

shorts.title: The three parts of a prompt
shorts.idea: An application sends instructions, context and the question together as one prompt.

shorts.title: A source in the prompt
shorts.idea: With the source in the context, the model answers from it and cites it.

shorts.title: Questions the source cannot answer
shorts.idea: The instructions tell the model to say when the context does not hold the answer.

shorts.title: Instructions for an ambiguous question
shorts.idea: Two sets of instructions give two different answers to the same ambiguous question.

shorts.title: A document collection and its metadata
shorts.idea: Metadata records what the text does not say about itself, such as the edition date.

shorts.title: Dividing documents into passages
shorts.idea: Passages that follow the sections of a document keep a figure with its context.

shorts.title: Passages as vectors
shorts.idea: An embedding model turns each passage into a vector, and passages close in meaning get close vectors.

shorts.title: Effects of poor preparation on answers
shorts.idea: Missing metadata and badly divided passages lead to wrong or undated answers.

shorts.title: Answering from a document archive
shorts.idea: The application finds passages for each question, and the model answers from them with a citation to each source.

shorts.title: How the search ranks passages
shorts.idea: The search ranks passages by closeness in meaning, and a needed passage can fall just below the cut.

shorts.title: Dates in the search
shorts.idea: The search does not know which report is the newest; a filter on the edition date does.

shorts.title: Questions outside the archive
shorts.idea: The instructions tell the model to say when the passages do not hold the answer.

shorts.title: Testing the search and checking answers
shorts.idea: Test questions check the search without the model, and the citation lets a reader check the answer.

shorts.title: Text search and a data tool
shorts.idea: A tool returns the figure from the data source, where text search returns passages that mention it.

shorts.title: A tool as described to the model
shorts.idea: The model sees a name, a description and the parameters of each tool.

shorts.title: Tool calls run by the application
shorts.idea: The model asks for a call, and the application runs the tool and returns the result.

shorts.title: Requests for data that does not exist
shorts.idea: A tool that returns no data lets the model say that the figure does not exist.

shorts.title: Answers in a fixed format
shorts.idea: A schema fixes the fields of the answer so that code can read it.

shorts.title: Tools over MCP
shorts.idea: The Model Context Protocol offers the same tool to any application that supports it.

shorts.title: A workflow with its order in code
shorts.idea: In a workflow, code fixes the order of the steps.

shorts.title: An agent that chooses its steps
shorts.idea: In an agent, the model chooses which tool to call next.

shorts.title: Failures of an agent
shorts.idea: An agent needs limits for a question no tool answers, a call that fails and a loop that does not end.

shorts.title: Choosing a workflow or an agent
shorts.idea: A fixed task suits a workflow, and an open task suits an agent with limits.

shorts.title: Claim tags on figures
shorts.idea: The model tags each figure with the id of the data it came from.

shorts.title: Flagged and untagged figures
shorts.idea: The verifier flags a tagged figure that differs from the data and marks a figure with no tag.

shorts.title: Scope of the figure check
shorts.idea: The check confirms each figure against the data, and the reader judges whether it answers the question.
